stem: A client with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, elevated serum creatinine, and proteinuric diabetic nephropathy is prescribed losartan. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Losartan has a labeled diabetic-nephropathy indication in this population and can reduce the rate of kidney-disease progression, including progression to doubling of serum creatinine or end-stage renal disease.
options.B: Losartan is contraindicated whenever chronic kidney disease is present because angiotensin-receptor blockers always accelerate renal failure.
options.C: Losartan is used only to lower blood pressure and has no labeled renal-outcome indication in type 2 diabetic nephropathy.
options.D: Losartan cures the underlying diabetic kidney disease, so renal-function and potassium monitoring are unnecessary after therapy begins.

rationale: Current FDA labeling indicates losartan for diabetic nephropathy with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension. In this population, losartan reduces the rate of progression of nephropathy as measured by doubling of serum creatinine or end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation. It does not cure CKD, and the label includes warnings regarding renal-function deterioration and hyperkalemia, so monitoring remains important. Therefore, A is correct; B, C, and D contradict the current prescribing information.
educational_objective: Recognize the labeled renal-protective indication of losartan in hypertensive type 2 diabetic nephropathy with proteinuria while understanding that treatment slows progression rather than curing CKD.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
source_document_title: LOSARTAN POTASSIUM tablets — Official Prescribing Information
source_locator: Section 1.3, Nephropathy in Type 2 Diabetic Patients: losartan is indicated for diabetic nephropathy with elevated serum creatinine and proteinuria in patients with type 2 diabetes and a history of hypertension; it reduces progression measured by doubling of serum creatinine or end-stage renal disease. Sections 5.3-5.4: renal-function deterioration and hyperkalemia are recognized safety concerns requiring clinical monitoring.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports losartan's drug-specific diabetic-nephropathy indication and renal-progression outcome while also supporting continued renal-function/potassium safety monitoring.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate appropriateness of medication therapy, understand expected outcomes, monitor medication-related laboratory values/adverse effects, and provide client education.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — losartan use in proteinuric diabetic nephropathy
correction_summary: Rebuilt the generic ARB/CKD-proteinuria source item into a drug-specific losartan question using a current June 2026 FDA label. This avoids overgeneralizing identical renal-outcome evidence to every ARB and tests the exact labeled population and outcome instead of a vague claim about glomerular pressure.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Losartan renal-protection indication in diabetic nephropathy
audit_findings.source_authority: Current official FDA labeling via DailyMed; KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline was also checked and remains the current global CKD standard in 2026 while a focused update is underway.
audit_findings.currentness: The selected losartan label was revised June 2026 and the KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline remains current at the audit date.

claim_by_claim.stem: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, elevated creatinine, and proteinuric diabetic nephropathy match the labeled population.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because Section 1.3 directly states the nephropathy indication and reduction in progression measured by doubling creatinine or ESRD.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because CKD/diabetic nephropathy is not a blanket contraindication and is an explicit labeled indication in the specified population.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because losartan has a labeled renal-outcome indication beyond blood-pressure lowering in this population.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because losartan slows progression rather than curing diabetic nephropathy, and renal function/potassium still require monitoring.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Uses exact labeled outcomes and avoids extrapolating a mechanism-based renal benefit to all ARBs or all CKD phenotypes.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to evidence-based ARB use in diabetic nephropathy.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests CKD contraindication misconception, C antihypertensive-only thinking, and D cure/monitoring misconception. Each is clinically plausible and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A reproduces the current label's population and renal outcome. No other option is partially equivalent.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe therapeutic role/outcomes of losartan in kidney disease and use comparable explanatory structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies is the strongest fit because the item tests medication indication, expected outcome, and safety monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited whether the item should stay generic to ACEi/ARB per KDIGO. Drug-specific labeling provides stronger exact support and removes class-level overgeneralization while preserving the source's renal-protection learning objective. No unresolved conflict remains.
